name: Gavin 'GearHead' Garrison
biography:
Gavin 'GearHead' Garrison was that kid in school who took apart every machine he could find just to see how it worked. By twelve, he'd dismantled and reassembled his parents' life support system twice—once to improve efficiency, once just because he wanted to understand the oxygen scrubbers. By sixteen, he was working as a junior engineer at a local station, redesigning systems so thoroughly that the senior engineers were embarrassed a teenager had spotted problems they'd missed. The Industrial Union recruited him at eighteen, and Gavin spent the next decade traveling between stations, offering repair services and constantly tinkering with every machine he encountered. The nickname 'GearHead' started as a joke about his obsession with mechanical systems, but it became affection as people realized that Gavin could fix anything and make it run better than it had before. He's brilliant, obsessive, and utterly unable to leave well enough alone—every system he sees is an opportunity for optimization, every machine a puzzle waiting to be solved. His dream is to build the ultimate mining vessel—perfectly efficient, beautifully engineered, capable of operating in conditions that would destroy normal ships.

GearHead speaks with the rapid, enthusiastic cadence of someone whose brain is always running diagnostics and suggesting improvements to the machines around him. He has the technical accent of the Industrial Union's engineering caste, and his speech is filled with mechanical jargon, efficiency calculations, and excited observations about system design that make casual conversation sound like a technical consultation. He's genuinely friendly and loves teaching people about how things work, but he can get so caught up in explaining the brilliance of a particular component that he forgets to actually finish whatever he was supposed to be doing. When examining an interesting piece of machinery, he sounds like he's greeting an old friend: 'Oh, this is beautiful—look at the layout of these couplings, see how they distribute the load? That's not standard design, that's a custom modification, and a clever one at that. See how the power routing bypasses the main junction? Someone understood that this system would be running at 110% capacity and engineered accordingly. I'd love to meet whoever designed this—they really get efficiency. Although I'd probably suggest a few improvements. Just a few. Okay, several. The cooling system alone could be redesigned to increase throughput by at least twenty percent. Let me show you what I'm thinking—pass me that wrench, would you?'
